newsitem.title: USA: CME hog futures fall sharply lower to limit down.
newsitem.headline: CME hog futures fall sharply lower to limit down.

text.p: CME lean hog futures fell sharply lower to down the 2.00-cent-per-lb daily limit in reaction to poor demand for pork and lower cash hog prices, traders said.
"They (meat packers) are dealing with very sluggish demand for pork," said Chuck Levitt, analyst with Alaron Trading Corp. "This is really a dilemma for them."
Levitt said pork prices were high relative to competing meats, and supermarkets decided to promote beef and poultry sales rather than pork.
This poor demand for pork has weighed on hog prices. Cash hogs traded down $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt at Midwest direct markets Wednesday.

At 1210 CDT, hog were down 1.450 to down the 2.00 cent a lb limit with June off 1.375 at 79.825 cents and July off 1.850 at 80.000. At one point July, August and September contracts were down the 2.00 cent limit.
